headline: Portland schools' $10.6 million energy-savings project with Trane, including solar, presented ahead of December votes
summary: Phase one would run during 2027, with about $600,000 in incentives and annual savings of just over $500,000. Facilities staff said solar depends on roof age and strength, and federal solar funding is projected to expire at the end of October. Early childhood staff presented a plan to add pre-K classrooms over three years, starting at Rowe and Lyseth. The committee also moved a 2018 pre-K resolution and a one-year staff pilot to the full board.
decisions: Moved the 2018 pre-K resolution reaffirmation to the full board, 3-0.
Moved the one-year pre-K pilot for up to 10 employee seats to the full board, 3-0.
discussion: Pre-K expansion costs: Staff said the district would add two classrooms a year, with about $30,000 per classroom for startup costs and possible state funding. Members asked how the budget would absorb the added costs.
Staff employee pre-K pilot: Members discussed whether the seat benefit is fair to other families, and staff said the 10-seat cap would be reassessed next year.
Energy savings guarantee: Staff said Trane must prove the savings to the district and the lender, and payments would never exceed annual savings.

Roof condition and solar: Staff said most roofs should be replaced every 25 years and several are overdue. Staff said solar over parking lots would cost about 40% more per panel, with a return over 20 years.

New CIP review schedule: Staff said the board asked for more time, so the first read is January 12th, second read January 26th, and vote February 9th. Members asked why the first and second reads are on separate days.

decision_evidence.quote: Um, so, for the 2018 resolution, I'd be looking for a motion to move that forward. ...And I am also a yes, so that motion passes.
I'd be looking for a motion to move that topic along to the full board as well. ...And I am also a yes, so that passes as well.
